response: Single-valve replacement can be a safe and effective treatment option for patients with prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) who have double prostheses, but it depends on various factors, including the location and extent of the infection, the condition of the unaffected valve, and the patient's overall health. In some cases, replacing only the infected valve may be sufficient, while in others, replacement of both valves may be necessary to ensure optimal outcomes and prevent further complications. The decision to perform single-valve replacement should be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the individual patient's needs and circumstances, and should be guided by a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals, including cardiologists, cardiothoracic surgeons, and infectious disease specialists.
